thesis: The bear carries the current-turnaround objection because savings and fibre growth have not outweighed lower quarterly EBIT and higher finance costs. Neutral recognizes modest H1 operating resilience and delivered savings without declaring the franchise impaired. A group recovery must show earnings conversion and funded cash after those pressures.
strongest_counterexample: RM141m operational savings, 47.2% Home & Fibre growth and H1 EBIT +0.6% establish concrete levers and some operating resilience rather than uniform contraction.
invalidation_conditions: A subsequent comparable quarter reports PAT growth above zero and no increase in net finance costs, with a positive reconciled post-investment cash result, reversing the latest earnings/funding objection.
A comparable subsequent H1 EBIT decline below zero would defeat the retained H1 operating-resilience counterweight.
evidence_gaps: Incremental recurring group-profit contribution of savings and fibre.
Financing costs, debt maturity profile and cash conversion.
decisive_factors: Q2 PAT -7.7% from lower EBIT and higher finance costs.
H1 EBIT +0.6% lags service revenue +1.5%; bearish chart has no confirmed reversal.
